name: Silvery Spinnerets
summary: Near Wellspring Lake, Silvery Spinnerets are sought for a rite honoring Lady Sathrah. Her silver webs once gathered healing evening dew for the Sisterhood of Elune in Darnassus.

sections.title: Sacred Webbing and Corruption
sections.body:
By moonlight near Wellspring Lake, Lady Sathrah spun shimmering webs. Her silver silk gathered evening mist into healing dew, prized by the Sisterhood of Elune in Darnassus.

Then corruption reached her in Teldrassil and drove her into violent madness. Sathrah threatened her brood and the surrounding forest. Priestess A'moora asks travelers to end her suffering and recover her spinnerets, showing mercy to a once-revered creature of the great boughs.

sections.title: A Sacrifice for Rebirth
sections.body: The Sisterhood offers the recovered spinnerets to Elune at the central fountain inside the Temple of the Moon. In the rite called Sathrah's Sacrifice, the priestesses pray that the Moon Goddess will receive the creature's spirit. They ask her to cleanse the madness that claimed Sathrah's mortal body and grant her peace in rebirth.

faq.q: Where do you get the Silvery Spinnerets?
faq.answer: Retrieve the Silvery Spinnerets from Lady Sathrah, a large spider near Wellspring Lake along Teldrassil's northern borders.

faq.q: Why does Priestess A'moora want the spinnerets?
faq.answer: Priestess A'moora seeks the spinnerets for a sacred sacrifice to Elune. The rite honors Lady Sathrah's former purity and asks the goddess to cleanse her spirit and grant her peace and rebirth.

faq.q: Why were Lady Sathrah's webs special?
faq.answer: Lady Sathrah spun luminous silver silk that caught evening mist beneath the moonlight. The dew held potent restorative magic, and the Sisterhood of Elune prized and stored it in the Temple of the Moon for healing.

faq.q: Why was Lady Sathrah killed if she was sacred?
faq.answer: Corruption drove Lady Sathrah into incurable madness, as it did other wildlife in Teldrassil. Her aggression endangered the forest and threatened her brood, so the priestesses judged slaying her a sorrowful act of mercy.

angles.text: Lady Sathrah's tragic end reminds the Kaldorei that even creatures beloved by Elune can fall to the affliction sickening Teldrassil.
For servants of Elune, retrieving the spinnerets is a sacred funeral rite. It asks the Mother Moon to redeem a creature rather than treat her death as mere extermination.
